questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Assertion: A boy touches a hot pan and pulls his hand back before he has had any thought of being burnt; the junction that makes this speed possible is formed in the spinal cord, and the information about the heat still goes on to reach the brain.
2. Reason: Nerves from all over the body meet in a bundle in the spinal cord on their way to the brain, so this is the first point at which the nerve that detects the heat and the nerve that moves the muscles can be joined.
Choose the correct option: (A) Both 1 and 2 are true and 2 is the correct explanation for 1 (B) Both 1 and 2 are true but 2 is not the correct explanation for 1 (C) 1 is true but 2 is false (D) Both 1 and 2 are false

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both 1 and 2 are true and 2 is the correct explanation for 1

evidence:
Nerves from all over the body meet in a bundle in the spinal
cord on their way to the brain. Reflex arcs are formed in this spinal cord
itself, although the information input also goes on to reach the brain.

If all of this is
to be done when we touch a hot object, it may take enough time for us to
get burnt!

options.B: Both 1 and 2 are true but 2 is not the correct explanation for 1

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Assertion: After finishing a full meal, a boy says he no longer feels hungry, and this is because a centre associated with hunger lies in a separate part of the fore-brain.
2. Reason: This hunger centre lies in the mid-brain, the region to which information is passed on for the motor areas that control the movement of voluntary muscles such as our leg muscles.
Choose the correct option: (A) Both 1 and 2 are true and 2 is the correct explanation for 1 (B) Both 1 and 2 are true but 2 is not the correct explanation for 1 (C) 1 is true but 2 is false (D) Both 1 and 2 are false

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Assertion: A student tracing the route by which a message from the brain reaches the leg muscles finds that the brain and the spinal cord together make up the peripheral nervous system.
2. Reason: The cranial nerves that arise from the brain are the nerves that carry messages between the central nervous system and the other parts of the body.
Choose the correct option: (A) Both 1 and 2 are true and 2 is the correct explanation for 1 (B) Both 1 and 2 are true but 2 is not the correct explanation for 1 (C) 1 is true but 2 is false (D) Both 1 and 2 are false

evidence:
The
brain and spinal cord constitute the central nervous system (Fig. 6.3).

The communication between
the central nervous system and the other parts of the body is facilitated
by the peripheral nervous system consisting of cranial nerves arising
from the brain and spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.

options.A: Both 1 and 2 are true and 2 is the correct explanation for 1
options.B: Both 1 and 2 are true but 2 is not the correct explanation for 1
